speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mucous membranes, and tiny red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand what is causing these symptoms, have you been diagnosed with any bleeding disorders or is there a family history of similar issues?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP). 

Given the history of frequent epistaxis, gum bleeding, and petechiae on the extremities in a 4-year-old male with no mention of family bleeding disorders, the clinical picture strongly suggests immune-mediated thrombocytopenia. 

REQUEST IMAGES: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Platelet Count.
